To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a set of 24 quality indicators for RM care was developed.
we have generated a set of indicators for the care of couples with recurrent miscarriage.

we developed a set of 22 valid quality indicators for recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) based on the Dutch guideline for RPL, that all evidence level A and D recommendations were accepted as indicators while 64% and 22% level B and C recommendations, respectively, were accepted as indicators.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of quality indicators for recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and the exploration of the relation between the strength of the evidence of the recommendations and the acceptance rate as a quality indicator.
developing and testing indicators to measure the quality of care for RM patients in daily clinical practice.
the development of valid quality indicators to monitor adherence to the guidelines in clinical practice and to improve quality of care delivered.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a set of 17 indicators (including 2 of the consensus-based recommendations) was selected.
the quality indicators are a good reflection of the guideline recommendations, and that the quality indicators can be applied in clinical practice to monitor quality of RM care.
a higher evidence level increases the chance of being accepted as a quality indicator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of care in RM can be measured by a set of 22 indicators, which are based on evidence-based guidelines.
the quality indicators are based on the Dutch guideline for RM, and that all recommendations of high and consensus evidence level are accepted as quality indicators.
the acceptance rate of recommendations as indicators was highest for recommendations of highest (level A) or lowest (level D) evidence level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acceptance rate of recommendations of evidence levels B and C as quality indicators is lower than expected.
the evidence level of a recommendation is a good indicator for its acceptance as quality indicator.
recommendations based on level A evidence were accepted as quality indicators in 100% of cases, while only 22% of recommendations based on level C evidence were accepted.
